items.title: Rankine--Hugoniot in space--time normal form
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, $T>0$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^n)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, a unit vector $\eta\in\mathbb R^n$, and distinct states $u_L,u_R\in\mathbb R$. Prescribe the Riemann datum $u_0(x)=u_L$ for $x\cdot\eta<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_R$ for $x\cdot\eta>0$, and for $0<t<T$ set $u(t,x)=u_L$ when $x\cdot\eta<ct$ and $u(t,x)=u_R$ when $x\cdot\eta>ct$. This bounded piecewise-constant function has strong local $L^1$ initial trace $u_0$ and is a distributional weak solution of $u_t+\operatorname{div}_x f(u)=0$ exactly when $$ igl(f(u_R)-f(u_L) igr)\cdot\eta=c\,(u_R-u_L).$$ The plane interface $\Gamma=\{(t,x):x\cdot\eta=ct\}$ has unit normal from the left side to the right side $
u=(-c,\eta)/\sqrt{1+c^2}$; hence the equivalent space--time normal equation is $$[u]
u_t+[f(u)]\cdot
u_x= rac{-c\,(u_R-u_L)+(f(u_R)-f(u_L))\cdot\eta}{\sqrt{1+c^2}}=0.$$ This direct plane calculation uses no division by the jump.
items.strategy:
Choose an index $k$ with $\eta_k
e0$ and solve the plane for $x_k=\gamma(t,x')=(ct-\sum_{j
e k}\eta_jx_j)/\eta_k$. If $\eta_k>0$, the minus side is $x_k<\gamma$; if $\eta_k<0$, it is $x_k>\gamma$. Apply Fubini to the weak test integral, which is compactly supported. On a subgraph, one-dimensional FTC in $x_k$ gives the normal contribution from the $x_k$ derivative; for each tangential variable $z_j$ (including $t$), differentiate $I_j(z')=\int_{-\infty}^{\gamma(z')}F_j\varphi\,dx_k$ under the integral sign (the smooth compact test supplies a uniform integrable majorant), use the chain rule for the endpoint, and integrate its compactly supported derivative to zero. The supergraph case has the opposite orientation. The interface contribution is therefore $-[F]\cdot N$ times the test trace in graph coordinates, where $F=(u,f(u))$ is the space--time flux and $N$ is the unnormalised normal from the minus side to the plus side. Since $
abla\gamma=(c/\eta_k,-\eta_{j
e k}/\eta_k)$, this normal is $N=(-c,\eta)/|\eta_k|$ in the chosen orientation, and $[F]\cdot N=(-c[u]+[f]\cdot\eta)/|\eta_k|$. The bottom boundary terms cancel the weak formulation's initial-data term. A finite product of translated one-dimensional bumps from [[ex-smooth-compactly-supported-bump]] is a nonnegative smooth compactly supported test positive on a small interface patch; products are smooth by [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], so it shows necessity; the same integration-by-parts calculation proves sufficiency. Thus the exact condition is $[f]\cdot\eta=c[u]$. This is a Fubini/one-dimensional FTC graph calculation and uses no divergence theorem or choice principle. S: [KL] §4.2, pp. 20--23 and [BCL] §2.2, pp. 11--14 support the one-dimensional jump identity; the planar extension is derived here.

items.title: The Kruzhkov entropy inequality across a shock
items.statement: Let $f(u)=\tfrac12u^2$, let $u_L>u_R$, and let $u$ be the shock of [[ex-burgers-shock-riemann-solution]] with speed $s=\frac{u_L+u_R}{2}$. For the Kruzhkov entropy $\eta_k(u)=|u-k|$ with flux $q_k(u)=\operatorname{sgn}(u-k)(f(u)-f(k))$, the entropy-production distribution in space--time is $$\partial_t\eta_k(u)+\partial_xq_k(u)=\bigl([q_k]-s[\eta_k]\bigr)\,\delta(x-st),$$ where $\delta(x-st)$ denotes the distribution paired by $\langle\delta(x-st),\varphi\rangle=\int\varphi(t,st)\,dt$ (equivalently, the density with respect to arclength on $\Gamma$ is divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$). Direct computation gives, for every $k\in\mathbb R$, $$[q_k]-s[\eta_k]=\begin{cases}0,&k\le u_R\text{ or }k\ge u_L,\\[2pt](k-u_R)(k-u_L)<0,&u_R<k<u_L,\end{cases}$$ so the distribution is nonpositive, with strict dissipation exactly for $u_R<k<u_L$. For $u_L=1$, $u_R=0$, $k=\tfrac12$, the coefficient is $-\tfrac14$.
items.strategy: Use $s=(u_L+u_R)/2$ and $q_k(u)=(u+k)|u-k|/2$. For $k\le u_R$ or $k\ge u_L$, direct subtraction gives zero; for $u_R<k<u_L$ it gives $(k-u_R)(k-u_L)$. The distributional coefficient multiplies $\delta(x-st)$ with $dt$ parameterization, so no arclength normalization is implicit. Its sign is the admissibility condition of [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]]. In the unit example, the flux jump is $-1/4$ and the entropy jump is zero. S: [KL] §5.5, Proposition 5.13, pp. 46--48; [BCL] §2.3, pp. 16--19.

items.title: The Hamilton--Jacobi primitive of a Burgers solution
items.statement: Let $f(u)=\tfrac12u^2$ and let $u$ be the Burgers rarefaction with Riemann data $u_0=\mathbf 1_{(0,\infty)}$ ([[ex-burgers-rarefaction-riemann-solution]]): $u(t,x)=0$ for $x\le0$, $u(t,x)=x/t$ for $0<x<t$, and $u(t,x)=1$ for $x\ge t$. Its normalized primitive is $$U(t,x)=\int_{-\infty}^x u(t,y)\,dy=\begin{cases}0,&x\le0,\\[2pt] x^2/(2t),&0<x<t,\\[2pt]x-t/2,&x\ge t.\end{cases}$$ For every $t>0$, $U$ is $C^1$ across both rays $x=0$ and $x=t$, satisfies $U_t+\tfrac12(U_x)^2=0$ pointwise, and has $U_x=u$. It is Lipschitz on $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, but $u_0\notin L^1(\mathbb R)$ and $U_0(x)=x_+$ is unbounded, so this is not an instance of the bounded-primitive correspondence theorem.
items.strategy: Integrating the three pieces of the fan gives the displayed formula. On x<0 the derivatives vanish; on 0<x<t they are U_t=-x^2/(2t^2), U_x=x/t; on x>t they are U_t=-1/2, U_x=1. The values and first derivatives match at the two rays, so the equation holds pointwise and U is C^1 for t>0. Correctly oriented viscosity tests and Fermat give equality in both inequalities. The gradient bound on each region and the explicit Lipschitz restrictions to the rays and initial line give global Lipschitz continuity. The current correspondence theorem is used to verify that the example falls outside both of its data cases. P: direct calculus and contact test. S: [KL] §§6.1–6.2, pp. 52–55.

items.title: The expansion shock is weak but not entropic
items.statement: Let $f(u)=\tfrac12u^2$ and let the Riemann data be $u_0(x)=0$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=1$ for $x>0$. The increasing-state jump with left state $u^-=0$, right state $u^+=1$, and speed $s=\frac12$ is $$u(t,x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<t/2,\\1,&x>t/2.\end{cases}$$ It is a distributional weak solution with those data because the Rankine--Hugoniot condition holds. It is not a Kruzhkov entropy solution: for the convex entropy $\eta(u)=\tfrac12u^2$ with flux $q(u)=\tfrac13u^3$, the jump production is $[q]-s[\eta]=\tfrac13-\tfrac14=\tfrac1{12}>0$. It also fails the Kruzhkov test $k=\tfrac12$: $q_k(0)=\tfrac18$, $q_k(1)=\tfrac38$, and $[\eta_k]=0$, so $[q_k]-s[\eta_k]=\tfrac14>0$. For the same Riemann data, [[ex-burgers-rarefaction-riemann-solution]] gives an entropy solution, so the Rankine--Hugoniot condition alone admits both the expansion shock and the entropy rarefaction.
items.strategy: The jump speed is $(f(1)-f(0))/(1-0)=1/2$, so [[thm-rankine-hugoniot-jump-condition]] gives the weak-solution jump condition. For $(\eta,q)=(u^2/2,u^3/3)$ the coefficient is $1/3-(1/2)(1/2)=1/12>0$, violating the required nonpositive entropy production; this also violates the chord condition in [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]]. For $k=1/2$, $q_k(0)=1/8$, $q_k(1)=3/8$, and both entropy values equal $1/2$, giving coefficient $1/4>0$ directly in the Kruzhkov family. The rarefaction [[ex-burgers-rarefaction-riemann-solution]] is the entropy solution for these same data. S: [KL] §5.1--5.2, pp. 32--40; [IVR] §12.1.2, pp. 352--353.

items.title: Rankine--Hugoniot alone does not give uniqueness
items.statement: Let $f(u)=\tfrac12u^2$ and let the Riemann data be $u_L=0$, $u_R=1$. Then both of the following are weak solutions of the same Cauchy problem: the expansion shock from [[cex-expansion-shock-is-weak-but-not-entropic]] and the rarefaction fan from [[ex-burgers-rarefaction-riemann-solution]], $$u_{\mathrm{shock}}(t,x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<t/2,\\ 1,&x>t/2,\end{cases}\qquad u_{\mathrm{fan}}(t,x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\le0,\\ x/t,&0<x<t,\\ 1,&x\ge t.\end{cases}$$ Only the fan is a Kruzhkov entropy solution ([[thm-riemann-solver-for-strictly-convex-scalar-flux]]); the shock violates the entropy inequality. Thus the Rankine--Hugoniot condition and the weak formulation do not by themselves determine the solution, and an entropy selection is indispensable.
items.strategy: Collect the two explicit weak solutions and invoke [[cor-uniqueness-comparison-and-order-preservation-for-entropy-solutions]] for uniqueness within the entropy class; the shock's non-admissibility is [[cex-expansion-shock-is-weak-but-not-entropic]]. S: [KL] \u00a74.3 and \u00a75.1, pp. 27--33; [IVR] \u00a712.1.2, pp. 352--353.

items.title: Pointwise shock values do not affect the weak solution
items.statement: Let $u$ be a bounded distributional weak solution of $u_t+f(u)_x=0$ on $\Pi_T$ that is piecewise $C^1$ with shock curve $\Gamma=\{x=s(t)\}$. For any bounded measurable $\theta:(0,T)\to\mathbb R$, define $\tilde u(t,x)=u(t,x)$ for $x\ne s(t)$ and $\tilde u(t,s(t))=\theta(t)$. Then $\tilde u=u$ almost everywhere and represents the same $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ class, so it has the same weak formulation and initial datum. More generally, any bounded measurable modification on a Lebesgue-null subset of $\Pi_T$ leaves the weak-solution class unchanged. Thus the weak formulation cannot determine pointwise values on a shock curve.
items.strategy: The shock curve is a Lebesgue-null subset of space--time. A bounded measurable reassignment on it preserves measurability and boundedness, and changes neither the $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ equivalence class nor any integral in the weak identity. The same argument applies to any bounded measurable modification on a null set. S: [KL] §4.1--4.2, pp. 18--23; [BCL] §2.1, p. 9.

items.title: The convex-flux Riemann formula fails for a nonconvex flux
items.statement: Let $f(u)=u^3$ and take the Riemann data $u_L=1$ for $x<0$, $u_R=-1$ for $x>0$. The single jump $$u(t,x)=\begin{cases}1,&x<t,\\-1,&x>t\end{cases}$$ has Rankine--Hugoniot speed $s=1$ and is a distributional weak solution with these data: integration by parts on the two sides leaves only the interface coefficient $s[u]-[f]=1(-2)-(-2)=0$. Its strong local $L^1$ trace is the stated datum because the discrepancy is supported on $0<x<t$ and has amplitude $2$. It is not a Kruzhkov entropy solution. For $k=-\tfrac12$, the Kruzhkov pair has $\eta_k(1)=\tfrac32$, $\eta_k(-1)=\tfrac12$, $q_k(1)=\tfrac98$, and $q_k(-1)=\tfrac78$, hence $$[q_k]-s[\eta_k]= -\tfrac14-(-1)=\tfrac34>0,$$ violating the required nonpositive entropy production. Equivalently, the chord from $(-1,-1)$ to $(1,1)$ is $z\mapsto z$, while $z^3-z>0$ on $(-1,0)$ and $z^3-z<0$ on $(0,1)$, so the graph fails the required one-sided condition in [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]]. The strictly convex Riemann solver theorem does not apply: $f''(u)=6u$ changes sign and $f'$ is not monotone on $[-1,1]$. Thus its formula does not extend to this nonconvex flux; the concave-hull construction gives the corresponding composite entropy wave.
items.strategy: The speed is $(f(-1)-f(1))/(-1-1)=1$, so $s[u]=[f]=-2$. To check the weak Cauchy identity directly, integrate by parts over $x<t$ and $x>t$; the only interior term is the interface coefficient $s[u]-[f]$, which vanishes, and the bottom term is canceled by the prescribed initial datum. The initial local $L^1$ discrepancy is at most $2t$. For $k=-1/2$, $q_k(1)=9/8$, $q_k(-1)=7/8$, $[\eta_k]=-1$, and the entropy production is $3/4>0$. The chord calculation independently violates the general shock criterion [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]]. Do not use the convex-only Lax corollary: its strict-convexity hypothesis fails for $u^3$. The concave-hull construction gives the corresponding composite wave. S: [KL] §6.3, Example 6.7 and concave-hull construction, pp. 55--58; [BCL] §3.1, pp. 21--24.

items.title: Distinct states with equal flux give a stationary weak discontinuity
items.statement: Let $f(u)=u^2$ and $u_L=1>u_R=-1$. Since $f(u_L)=f(u_R)=1$, the Rankine--Hugoniot speed of the jump is $s=\dfrac{f(u_R)-f(u_L)}{u_R-u_L}=0$: the function $u(t,x)=1$ for $x<0$ and $u(t,x)=-1$ for $x>0$ is a stationary weak solution of $u_t+(u^2)_x=0$ with the corresponding Riemann data. It is also entropic: the chord condition of [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]] with $u^-=1>u^+=-1$ requires the graph of $f(u)=u^2$ on $[-1,1]$ to lie below the chord through the endpoints, and that chord is the constant line $1$, with $u^2\le1$ throughout. Thus $f(u_L)=f(u_R)$ yields a zero-speed admissible shock; admissibility was a separate check and did not follow from the jump condition.
items.strategy: The jump condition gives $s=0$ because the flux values coincide; weak solvability follows from [[thm-rankine-hugoniot-jump-condition]]. Admissibility is checked by the chord condition of [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]]: the relevant chord is horizontal at height $1$ and the parabola $u^2$ lies below it on $[-1,1]$. S: [KL] \u00a75.1--5.2, pp. 31--40; [BCL] \u00a72.3, pp. 16--19.

items.title: Affine flux reduces the entropy semigroup to translation
items.statement: Assume countable choice and dependent choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]), as used by the translation-continuity and entropy-semigroup results below. Let $f(u)=cu+d$, with $c,d\in\mathbb R$, and let $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R)$. The entropy solution is $$u(t,x)=u_0(x-ct).$$ For every convex entropy pair $(\eta,q)$, $q'(u)=c\eta'(u)$, hence $q(u)=c\eta(u)+C$; the transport change of variables gives $$\partial_t\eta(u)+\partial_xq(u)=0$$ in distributions, so entropy production is zero. Any jump already present in $u_0$ translates at speed $c$ with the same left and right states and zero production $[q]-c[\eta]=0$; the affine evolution creates no new shocks. In particular the semigroup of [[thm-entropy-solution-semigroup-on-lone]] is $S_tu_0=u_0(\cdot-ct)$.
items.strategy: Let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R\times(0,T))$ and set $\psi(t,y)=\varphi(t,y+ct)$. Then $\psi_t=\varphi_t(t,y+ct)+c\varphi_x(t,y+ct)$ by [[thm-chain-rule]]. Translation preserves Lebesgue measure ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]], [[def-measure-preserving-transformation-and-system]], [[thm-integrals-are-invariant-under-measure-preserving-maps]]); Fubini and FTC therefore reduce the weak transport identity for $u_0(x-ct)$ to $\int u_0(y)\psi_t(t,y)\,dy\,dt=0$. The constant flux term $d$ integrates to zero against $\varphi_x$. Including a test that meets $t=0$, the same calculation leaves $\int u_0(y)\psi(0,y)\,dy$, exactly canceled by the initial-data term, so this is a weak solution with datum $u_0$. For each convex entropy pair, $q=c\eta+C$ and the same distributional transport calculation applied to $\eta(u_0)$ gives zero production. The $L^1$ translation-continuity theorem ([[thm-translation-is-continuous-in-l-p-for-one-le-p-less-infinity]]) gives the strong initial trace; hence the profile is the entropy solution and equals $S_tu_0$ by the uniqueness built into [[thm-entropy-solution-semigroup-on-lone]]. For a datum with a jump $a\to b$, its translate remains a jump $a\to b$ and $[q]-c[\eta]=0$. S: [KR] §5, remarks on linear equations and the degenerate case, pp. 239--241; [BCL] §3.1, linear-flux Riemann solution, pp. 21--22.

items.title: Nonconvex Riemann data can require a composite shock--rarefaction wave
items.statement: Let $f(u)=u^3$ and take the Riemann data $u_L=1$ for $x<0$, $u_R=-1$ for $x>0$ as in [[cex-convex-flux-riemann-formula-fails-for-a-nonconvex-flux]]. The entropy profile is $$u(t,x)=\begin{cases}1,&x<\tfrac34t,\\[3pt]-\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3t}},&\tfrac34t<x<3t,\\[3pt]-1,&x\ge3t.\end{cases}$$ It consists of an admissible shock $1\to-\tfrac12$ at speed $3/4$ and a centred rarefaction on the strictly concave flux interval $[-1,-\tfrac12]$, followed by the constant state $-1$. The shock chord residual factors as $$f(z)-f(1)-\tfrac34(z-1)=(z-1)(z+\tfrac12)^2\le0\quad(-\tfrac12\le z\le1),$$ so the general entropy chord criterion gives admissibility. On the concave interval, $f'(u)=3u^2$ is strictly decreasing and its inverse is $\psi(\xi)=-\sqrt{\xi/3}$ for $3/4\le\xi\le3$; hence the fan solves the equation pointwise and all entropy productions vanish there. The traces match continuously at $x=3t$, and the initial trace is the stated Riemann datum. The concave-hull prescription consists of the cubic arc on $[-1,-\tfrac12]$ followed by the chord from $(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac18)$ to $(1,1)$.
items.strategy: Tangency of the chord from $(1,1)$ to $f(z)=z^3$ at $\hat u=-1/2$ gives shock speed $s=(1-(-1/8))/(1-(-1/2))=3/4$. Across the descending jump $1\to-1/2$, Rankine--Hugoniot holds. To verify the weak Cauchy identity, integrate the test expression on the constant left region, the fan, and the constant right region; the interface coefficient $s[u]-[f]$ vanishes at the shock, while the traces match at the fan's right edge $x=3t$. The bottom term is canceled by the initial datum. The shock residual factors as $(z-1)(z+1/2)^2\le0$ on $[-1/2,1]$; since $[u]=-3/2<0$, the product in [[lem-convex-entropy-condition-for-a-shock-is-the-flux-chord-inequality]] is nonnegative. For the fan, $\psi(\xi)=-\sqrt{\xi/3}$ is the smooth inverse of the strictly decreasing $f'$ on $[-1,-1/2]$. With $\xi=x/t$, $u_t+f'(u)u_x=\psi'(\xi)(-\xi/t+f'(\psi(\xi))/t)=0$; the fan is locally Lipschitz on $t>0$, continuous at both edges, so the chain rule yields zero entropy production there. The profile differs from the initial step only on $0<x<3t$, with amplitude at most $2$, hence its local $L^1$ trace is the prescribed datum. Uniqueness of the entropy solution follows from [[cor-uniqueness-comparison-and-order-preservation-for-entropy-solutions]]. This direct concave-segment proof does not invoke the strictly convex Riemann solver or convex Lax criterion. S: [KL] §6.3, Example 6.7, pp. 55--57; [BCL] §3.1, pp. 21--26.
